sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 10.0% a year from $129 billion in FY2017 to $303 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F203].
Operating income grew faster at 12.3% and net income at 14.7%, lifting operating margin from 3.2% to 3.9% [F204][F205][F23][F32].
FY2021 was the first inflection, with revenue up 17.5% on a 16% comparable-sales increase driven by shopping frequency, average ticket and strong non-foods and e-commerce sales [D189][P54][P56].
FY2022 was the second, revenue up 15.8% as comparable sales rose 14%, with the strongest growth in gasoline, business centers and travel amid inflation [D238][P42].
Growth then slowed to 6.8% in FY2023 before re-accelerating to 10.1% in FY2026 [D287][D434].
The US segment supplied 72.5% of FY2026 revenue and contributed 7.2pp of the 10.1% growth [D670][D672][D434].
FY2026 net sales rose $27.3 billion, of which comparable sales added $22.5 billion on a 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping frequency [P14].
Food and Sundries remained the largest product line at 38.5% of revenue but contributed only 2.6pp, while warehouse ancillary and other businesses added 3.7pp [D558][D560][D601].
Membership fees grew 11.0% to $5.9 billion on new sign-ups, fee increases and Executive upgrades [D664][S78][P13].
Incremental operating margin was 4.7% in FY2026, so profit grew faster than revenue, and diluted EPS rose 14.0% against 13.9% net income growth with a flat share count [D457][D438][D436][D452].
Operating margin of 3.9% is the window high, against a 3.4% median and a 3.1% low in FY2019 [F32][D691][D692][D690].
FY2026 margin rose 0.1pp, with SG&A adding 0.1pp and cost of revenue flat [D447][D460][D459].
SG&A fell 10 basis points as a share of sales, though excluding gasoline inflation it rose one basis point, with currency moves adding expense [P9].
Gross margin fell three basis points, with IEEPA tariff refunds adding three basis points and a sales-mix shift into ancillary businesses helping that line [P12].
Net margin of 3.0% is also the window high, helped by a 24.7% effective tax rate against 32.8% in FY2017 [F52][D694][D420][D8].
Operating cash flow of $15.8 billion was 1.71x net income, and free cash flow of $9.4 billion was 1.02x, against a 0.99x window median [F82][F42][D421][F102][D422][D701].
The FY2026 increase was mainly higher operating income plus a reduced net investment in inventories from faster turns and improved supplier payment terms [P6].
Free cash flow margin of 3.1% sits above the 2.8% median but below the 3.6% FY2020 high [D418][D698][D697].
Capex of $6.4 billion was 2.1% of revenue and 2.41x D&A, the highest multiple in the window [F92][F10][D417][D423].
Net cash reached $15.1 billion, or 5.0% of revenue, the 100th percentile against six retail peers whose median is -4.4% [D427][D428][D715][D716].
Long-term debt fell 31.5% to $3.9 billion while cash and investments rose 39.4% to $21.3 billion [D445][F192][D453][D425].
FY2026 financing outflow of $3.4 billion covered dividends, buybacks and debt repayment [F122][P4].
Buybacks and dividends of $3.3 billion were 35.2% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count was essentially flat at 444.4 million [D429][D430][X100].
Operating margin of 3.9% ranks in the 17th percentile against six retail peers whose median is 5.0%, so the model runs on volume rather than margin [F32][D709][D710].
Capex has grown 11.1% a year against 10.0% revenue growth, pushing the capex-to-D&A ratio to 2.41x and free cash flow conversion to 1.02x from a 1.58x window high [F209][F203][D423][D422][D700].
Current ratio of 1.06x is thin against a 1.13x window high, and current liabilities jumped 18.4% in FY2026 [F182][D703][D446].
Receivables grew 23.6% in FY2026, well ahead of 10.1% revenue growth, lifting days sales outstanding to 5 days from 4 [D455][D434][D431][D382].
Whether operating margin holds at or above the 3.9% FY2026 high or slips toward the 3.4% median, reported in the FY2027 10-K [F32][D691][D692].
Whether free cash flow per dollar of net income recovers toward the 0.99x median from 1.02x, or capex keeps the capex-to-D&A ratio above 2.41x [D422][D701][D423].
Whether membership fee growth holds above the 11.0% FY2026 rate, given the fee increase the filing expects to add revenue over the next two years [D664][P25].
